messages:
maria: quick pulse-check — when an upstream model node dies midstream, do we want the edge to buffer & attempt transparent resume, or fast-fail and push retry responsibility to clients?

sam: both sides have pros. resume = better UX, fewer client retries. con: more state in edge, harder to reason about billing and memory.

jin: resume helps continuity for conversations. main risk: if failover lands on a different model version/quantization we can get inconsistent outputs. need strict compatibility checks.

kevin: ops POV: unbounded buffering killed our POC (OOM storm with many long polls). any resume approach MUST have strict per-conn caps + eviction policy. also, cost accounting: replayed tokens can cause double billing unless we detect/reconcile.

maria: propose a middle path: small prefix cache + short resume window. defaults conservative for hosted, configurable on dedicated. e.g. 8s / 4KB prefix / 128KB max-per-conn. fallback = fast-fail.

sam: rough config draft:
```
edge.retry.resume_window_secs = 8
edge.retry.prefix_bytes = 4096
edge.retry.max_buffer_per_conn = 131072  # bytes
edge.retry.require_model_fingerprint = true
edge.retry.fallback = "fast_fail"
```

jin: require_model_fingerprint true is crucial. fingerprint = hash(model_name + version + quant + request_schema). otherwise refuse resume and return a structured error for client to decide.

kevin: metrics we should emit: edge.resume.attempts, edge.resume.success, edge.buffer.evictions, edge.resume.incompatible_model, edge.billing.replay_events. Alert if resume.success / attempts < 0.8 after rollouts.

maria: streaming contract idea: attach monotonic chunk ids to frames so downstream proxies/clients can dedupe when resume causes overlap. also append a small JSON trailer when resume happens: {"resumed": true, "resume_gap_bytes": N, "from_fingerprint": "abc123"}. clients can surface this.

sam: agree. chunk ids should be 64-bit monotonic per-request. for HTTP streaming we can send chunk headers: `X-Edge-Chunk-Id: 12345`. keep it simple.

kevin: failure modes to document in RFC: 1) resume token persisted but KV flush failed -> token invalid; 2) client already received partial data then reconnects -> need dedupe; 3) model side-effects midstream (webhook/db) -> resume unsafe by default.

jin: call out side-effects: default resume=false for routes flagged as side-effecting. customers can opt-in if their backends are idempotent / support exactly-once semantics.

maria: action items: sam -> write RFC with config names + per-tenant overrides; kevin -> memory/cap limits + metrics + alerts; jin -> client contract (chunk ids + resume trailer + error codes). I'll collect examples for dedicated vs hosted defaults.

deploy-bot: RFC draft created by sam: https://go/repo/edge-resume-rfc (internal) — scheduled review Wed 11am.

kevin: one more note: for dedicated tenants we can expose larger windows and retention. but enforce absolute cap to avoid host instability. Recommend per-tenant quota and a soft-limited eviction policy (LRU by request age).

maria: makes sense. thanks all. follow-up sync Wed. :thumbsup:
